Why Some Companies Are Abandoning Open-Plan Offices

For two decades, open-plan layouts were promoted as a way of encouraging collaboration and reducing property costs. [1] A growing body of research now suggests that the benefits were overstated. In a study of four hundred employees, researchers found that face-to-face interaction actually fell by about a third after a move to open-plan space, as staff retreated behind headphones to avoid distraction.

Some firms have [2] their strategy accordingly. Pemberton Partners recently converted half of its floor space into small rooms for concentrated work, [3] retaining shared areas for meetings. Its managing director says that productivity has improved, [4] she acknowledges that the evidence is anecdotal.

choices: The assumption behind the design was that proximity would naturally lead to conversation and to the exchange of ideas.
The assumption behind the design was that privacy would naturally lead to conversation and to the exchange of rooms.
The assumption behind the research was that proximity would naturally lead to distraction and to the exchange of headphones.
The design behind the assumption was that conversation would naturally lead to proximity and to the exchange of ideas.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says research suggests that the benefits were overstated, which presupposes an earlier assumption about collaboration; only the first states it.
Firms 'revised' their strategy, meaning changed it; 'reversed' would imply a complete opposite, and 'reviewed' only means examined.
'While retaining shared areas for meetings' contrasts the conversion with the retention of shared areas.
'Although she acknowledges that the evidence is anecdotal' concedes a limit before the claim; the others do not fit.

text:
Dear Ms. Whitcombe,

I write on behalf of the Marlowe Heritage Trust to thank you for your generous donation of £5,000 toward the restoration of the old market hall. Your contribution brings the total raised to £182,000, [1] means that we are now within sight of our target of £250,000.

[2] Work on the roof is due to begin in April, and we hope that the hall will reopen to the public in the autumn of next year. Donors who contribute £1,000 or more will be invited to a private viewing, [3] their names will be recorded on a plaque in the entrance hall. We shall [4] you informed of progress through our quarterly newsletter.

Yours sincerely,
Alistair Penn
Director

questions.explanation: 'Which means that we are now within sight of our target' refers to the whole preceding fact; the others cannot do this.

choices: Your generosity has made it impossible to move from planning to action sooner than we had dared to hope.
Your generosity has made it possible to move from planning to action sooner than we had dared to hope.
Our generosity has made it possible to move from action to planning sooner than you had dared to hope.
Your generosity made it possible to move from planning to action sooner than we had dared to hope.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says work on the roof is due to begin in April, so the previous one must say that donations have enabled progress; the others negate it, reverse the actors, or use a past tense.
'And their names will be recorded' adds a further benefit to the invitation; the others express contrast.
After 'shall', the base verb 'keep' is required in 'keep you informed'.

text:
Thornbury Business Centre – Serviced Offices

For companies in need of flexible space without the burden of a long lease, Thornbury offers fully furnished offices on terms of one month or longer. Rates include utilities, high-speed internet and use of the reception service, [1] tenants avoid the hidden costs that so often accompany conventional rentals.

[2] Meeting rooms, which seat from four to twenty people, can be booked by the hour through our online portal. [3] a tenant's needs change, the office can be exchanged for a larger or smaller one on thirty days' notice, [4] penalty. Viewings are available on weekdays between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m.

questions.explanation: 'So that tenants avoid the hidden costs' states the purpose of all-inclusive rates; the others do not fit.

choices: The center is equipped for the needs of both large corporations and established firms with several hundred staff.
The center is equipped for the needs of both small start-ups and established firms with a handful of staff.
The center was equipped for the needs of both small start-ups and established firms with a handful of staff.
The start-ups are equipped for the needs of both the center and the established firms with a handful of staff.
questions.explanation: The next sentence is about meeting rooms that seat four to twenty, consistent with small tenants; only the first fits. The others mention large corporations, a past tense, or confuse the subjects.
'Should a tenant's needs change' is an inverted conditional with a singular subject and base form 'change'; the others cannot introduce it.
'Without penalty' means with no penalty; the others change the meaning.
